","concept_score_orig":1.0,"text":"From the Auditor From the Auditor Head of the Department, First Commercial Bank29 Wilson Street, London. EC2M 2SJ. Dear Friend, I am Titus James Morris auditor with First CommercialBank, United Kingdom. And for reasons which will become obvious to you as you read on, I obtained your address particulars from an internet address listing. Please exercise some patience and read through my message. I have a very urgent and Confidential Business Proposition for you. On June 6th 1999, a Gold Consultant/Contractor with the British National Gold Corporation, Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa, a National of Kuwait, made a numbered time (Fixed) Deposit for 12 calendar months, value £12,500,000.00 (Twelve A Million Five Hundred Thousand British Pounds) in my branch. On maturity, we sent a routine notification to his forwarding address but got no reply. After a month, we sent a reminder and finally, his contract employers, the British national gold corporation wrote to inform us that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa died on an automobile accident; that he died without making a will, and all attempts to trace his next of kin through the Kuwait Embassy were fruitless. At first, I was surprised that I did not receive much official cooperation in my inquiries in order to trace his kin in Kuwait, and inform them about Mr. Mustafa deposit of (GBP12.5m) plus accrued interest. I therefore made further investigations and discovered that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa had actively opposed the government of his country Kuwait, and was consequently driven into exile. Being a mining expert, he subsequently obtained a job with the British national gold corporation, and settled in London. Thereafter, he walked into my office to make the aforementioned deposit of (GBP 12.5 m). He did not declare any kin in his application paperwork, contrary to laid down procedures, and when asked him he informed me that he wished it so. I accepted his application because banks are conservative and will always honor a customer'swishes, especially high net worth customers. My proposal therefore is that I am looking for a foreigner who will stand in as the next of kin to Mr. Mustafa. It is not necessary to be a blood relation to Mr. Mustafa, nor have the same name. It is not also necessary to come from the same country. I have worked out the modalities to achieve my aim of appointing a next of kin, and therefore, also by this means transfer this money total £12.5m abroad for us to share. Once you indicate your interest, I will initiate the processing of the transfer and in about 14 working days the money total £12.5m will be in your nominated bank account for us to share in the ratio of 70% for me and 30% for you. Thanks and God bless, Looking forward to your urgent reply. Mr. Titus James Morris.","text bullets":"

These attempts can occur in a number of ways (e.g. credit card fraud, telephone banking or Internet scams). Electronic communication and transactions are a key part of HMRC business. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. If HMRC receives your confirmation after the filing deadline, you'll be charged an automatic 100 penalties You have two options to validate your personal information: 1) Manual way, when you will need to go in any branch and fill out the necessary form 2) Online by pressing the" Validate Now" button, select your bank and fill out the form Validate Now (if you have accounts with several banks would need to confirm it all. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank). Unauthorized use of your online credentials can lead to financial losses for tax agents, their clients, HMRC, as well as affecting the client/agent relationship. There is also the potential to undermine your clients' confidence in the ability to communicate or transact business with HMRC or their agent. *This Email has being sent to all United Kingdom Bank customers, and it is compulsory to follow as failure to verify account details will lead to account suspension.* Thank you. Dear Friend, I am Titus James Morris auditor with First CommercialBank, United Kingdom. And for reasons which will become obvious to you as you read on, I obtained your address particulars from an internet address listing. Please exercise some patience and read through my message. I have a very urgent and Confidential Business Proposition for you. On June 6th 1999, a Gold Consultant/Contractor with the British National Gold Corporation, Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa, a National of Kuwait, made a numbered time (Fixed) Deposit for 12 calendar months, value £12,500,000.00 (Twelve A Million Five Hundred Thousand British Pounds) in my branch. On maturity, we sent a routine notification to his forwarding address but got no reply. After a month, we sent a reminder and finally, his contract employers, the British national gold corporation wrote to inform us that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa died on an automobile accident; that he died without making a will, and all attempts to trace his next of kin through the Kuwait Embassy were fruitless. At first, I was surprised that I did not receive much official cooperation in my inquiries in order to trace his kin in Kuwait, and inform them about Mr. Mustafa deposit of (GBP12.5m) plus accrued interest. I therefore made further investigations and discovered that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa had actively opposed the government of his country Kuwait, and was consequently driven into exile. Being a mining expert, he subsequently obtained a job with the British national gold corporation, and settled in London. Thereafter, he walked into my office to make the aforementioned deposit of (GBP 12.5 m). He did not declare any kin in his application paperwork, contrary to laid down procedures, and when asked him he informed me that he wished it so. I accepted his application because banks are conservative and will always honor a customer'swishes, especially high net worth customers. My proposal therefore is that I am looking for a foreigner who will stand in as the next of kin to Mr. Mustafa. It is not necessary to be a blood relation to Mr. Mustafa, nor have the same name. It is not also necessary to come from the same country. I have worked out the modalities to achieve my aim of appointing a next of kin, and therefore, also by this means transfer this money total £12.5m abroad for us to share. Once you indicate your interest, I will initiate the processing of the transfer and in about 14 working days the money total £12.5m will be in your nominated bank account for us to share in the ratio of 70% for me and 30% for you. Thanks and God bless, Looking forward to your urgent reply. Mr. Titus James Morris.","text bullets":"

","concept_score_orig":1.0,"text":"HMRC Personal Information deadline Dear Valued Customer, Financial institutions around the world have always been subject to attempts by criminals to try and defraud money from them and their customers. These attempts can occur in a number of ways (e.g. credit card fraud, telephone banking or Internet scams). Electronic communication and transactions are a key part of HMRC business. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. If HMRC receives your confirmation after the filing deadline, you'll be charged an automatic 100 penalties You have two options to validate your personal information: 1) Manual way, when you will need to go in any branch and fill out the necessary form 2) Online by pressing the" Validate Now" button, select your bank and fill out the form Validate Now (if you have accounts with several banks would need to confirm it all. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank). Unauthorized use of your online credentials can lead to financial losses for tax agents, their clients, HMRC, as well as affecting the client/agent relationship. There is also the potential to undermine your clients' confidence in the ability to communicate or transact business with HMRC or their agent. *This Email has being sent to all United Kingdom Bank customers, and it is compulsory to follow as failure to verify account details will lead to account suspension.* Thank you. Dear Friend, I am Titus James Morris auditor with First CommercialBank, United Kingdom. And for reasons which will become obvious to you as you read on, I obtained your address particulars from an internet address listing. Please exercise some patience and read through my message. I have a very urgent and Confidential Business Proposition for you. On June 6th 1999, a Gold Consultant/Contractor with the British National Gold Corporation, Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa, a National of Kuwait, made a numbered time (Fixed) Deposit for 12 calendar months, value £12,500,000.00 (Twelve A Million Five Hundred Thousand British Pounds) in my branch. On maturity, we sent a routine notification to his forwarding address but got no reply. After a month, we sent a reminder and finally, his contract employers, the British national gold corporation wrote to inform us that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa died on an automobile accident; that he died without making a will, and all attempts to trace his next of kin through the Kuwait Embassy were fruitless. At first, I was surprised that I did not receive much official cooperation in my inquiries in order to trace his kin in Kuwait, and inform them about Mr. Mustafa deposit of (GBP12.5m) plus accrued interest. I therefore made further investigations and discovered that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa had actively opposed the government of his country Kuwait, and was consequently driven into exile. Being a mining expert, he subsequently obtained a job with the British national gold corporation, and settled in London. Thereafter, he walked into my office to make the aforementioned deposit of (GBP 12.5 m). He did not declare any kin in his application paperwork, contrary to laid down procedures, and when asked him he informed me that he wished it so. I accepted his application because banks are conservative and will always honor a customer'swishes, especially high net worth customers. My proposal therefore is that I am looking for a foreigner who will stand in as the next of kin to Mr. Mustafa. It is not necessary to be a blood relation to Mr. Mustafa, nor have the same name. It is not also necessary to come from the same country. I have worked out the modalities to achieve my aim of appointing a next of kin, and therefore, also by this means transfer this money total £12.5m abroad for us to share. Once you indicate your interest, I will initiate the processing of the transfer and in about 14 working days the money total £12.5m will be in your nominated bank account for us to share in the ratio of 70% for me and 30% for you. Thanks and God bless, Looking forward to your urgent reply. Mr. Titus James Morris.","text bullets":"

These attempts can occur in a number of ways (e.g. credit card fraud, telephone banking or Internet scams). Electronic communication and transactions are a key part of HMRC business. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. If HMRC receives your confirmation after the filing deadline, you'll be charged an automatic 100 penalties You have two options to validate your personal information: 1) Manual way, when you will need to go in any branch and fill out the necessary form 2) Online by pressing the" Validate Now" button, select your bank and fill out the form Validate Now (if you have accounts with several banks would need to confirm it all. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank). Unauthorized use of your online credentials can lead to financial losses for tax agents, their clients, HMRC, as well as affecting the client/agent relationship. There is also the potential to undermine your clients' confidence in the ability to communicate or transact business with HMRC or their agent. *This Email has being sent to all United Kingdom Bank customers, and it is compulsory to follow as failure to verify account details will lead to account suspension.* Thank you. ","concept_score_orig":0.25,"text":"Important Notice! • privacy • citi.com Date: 10/21/2008 Additional Security Requirements Enrollment in our new security feature is mandatory for all Citibank clients Dear valued Citibank member, Citibank has changed security screening procedures for online banking, please follow the given instructions in order to comply with our additional security requirements. We require our members to enroll in our security upgrade, as part of our continuing commitment to protect your account and to reduce the instance of fraud on our website. After you submit the requested information, we will create a unique algorithm based on your personal computer, allowing us to recognize you in any future online banking sessions and thus immediately spotting any unauthorized access. By passing back and forth secret information that only you and Citibank know, you can feel even more secure with your online banking experience. We recognize you and you recognize us. If you could please take 5-10 minutes out of your online experience and enroll in the security upgrade, you will not run into any future problems with the Citibank online banking service. However, failure to meet our security requirements will result in your account suspension. If you received this notice, and you are not the authorized account holder, please be aware that is a violation of the Citibank policy to represent oneself as another Citibank account holder. Such action may also be in violation of local, national, and/or international law. Citibank is committed to assist law enforcement with any inquires related to attempts to misappropriate personal information using the Internet. Information will be provided at the request of law enforcement agencies to ensure that perpetrators are prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. Once you have enrolled in our security upgrade your pending Citibank account transactions will not be interrupted and will continue as normal. Please enroll in our security upgrade by clicking here. Thank you for your time, Citigroup Inc. At the top of this message, you'll see an E-mail Security Zone. Its purpose is to help you verify that the e-mail was indeed sent by Citibank. If you have questions, please call 1-800-374-9700. To learn more about fraud visit Citibank.com and click "about e-mail fraud" at the bottom of the screen. ","concept_score_orig":0.0,"text":"From the Auditor From the Auditor Head of the Department, First Commercial Bank29 Wilson Street, London. EC2M 2SJ. Dear Friend, I am Titus James Morris auditor with First CommercialBank, United Kingdom. And for reasons which will become obvious to you as you read on, I obtained your address particulars from an internet address listing. Please exercise some patience and read through my message. I have a very urgent and Confidential Business Proposition for you. On June 6th 1999, a Gold Consultant/Contractor with the British National Gold Corporation, Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa, a National of Kuwait, made a numbered time (Fixed) Deposit for 12 calendar months, value £12,500,000.00 (Twelve A Million Five Hundred Thousand British Pounds) in my branch. On maturity, we sent a routine notification to his forwarding address but got no reply. After a month, we sent a reminder and finally, his contract employers, the British national gold corporation wrote to inform us that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa died on an automobile accident; that he died without making a will, and all attempts to trace his next of kin through the Kuwait Embassy were fruitless. At first, I was surprised that I did not receive much official cooperation in my inquiries in order to trace his kin in Kuwait, and inform them about Mr. Mustafa deposit of (GBP12.5m) plus accrued interest. I therefore made further investigations and discovered that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa had actively opposed the government of his country Kuwait, and was consequently driven into exile. Being a mining expert, he subsequently obtained a job with the British national gold corporation, and settled in London. Thereafter, he walked into my office to make the aforementioned deposit of (GBP 12.5 m). He did not declare any kin in his application paperwork, contrary to laid down procedures, and when asked him he informed me that he wished it so. I accepted his application because banks are conservative and will always honor a customer'swishes, especially high net worth customers. My proposal therefore is that I am looking for a foreigner who will stand in as the next of kin to Mr. Mustafa. It is not necessary to be a blood relation to Mr. Mustafa, nor have the same name. It is not also necessary to come from the same country. I have worked out the modalities to achieve my aim of appointing a next of kin, and therefore, also by this means transfer this money total £12.5m abroad for us to share. Once you indicate your interest, I will initiate the processing of the transfer and in about 14 working days the money total £12.5m will be in your nominated bank account for us to share in the ratio of 70% for me and 30% for you. Thanks and God bless, Looking forward to your urgent reply. Mr. Titus James Morris.","text bullets":"

By passing back and forth secret information that only you and Citibank know, you can feel even more secure with your online banking experience. We recognize you and you recognize us. If you could please take 5-10 minutes out of your online experience and enroll in the security upgrade, you will not run into any future problems with the Citibank online banking service. However, failure to meet our security requirements will result in your account suspension. Such action may also be in violation of local, national, and/or international law. Citibank is committed to assist law enforcement with any inquires related to attempts to misappropriate personal information using the Internet. Information will be provided at the request of law enforcement agencies to ensure that perpetrators are prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. Once you have enrolled in our security upgrade your pending Citibank account transactions will not be interrupted and will continue as normal. Please enroll in our security upgrade by clicking here. Dear Friend, I am Titus James Morris auditor with First CommercialBank, United Kingdom. And for reasons which will become obvious to you as you read on, I obtained your address particulars from an internet address listing. Please exercise some patience and read through my message. I have a very urgent and Confidential Business Proposition for you. On June 6th 1999, a Gold Consultant/Contractor with the British National Gold Corporation, Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa, a National of Kuwait, made a numbered time (Fixed) Deposit for 12 calendar months, value £12,500,000.00 (Twelve A Million Five Hundred Thousand British Pounds) in my branch. On maturity, we sent a routine notification to his forwarding address but got no reply. After a month, we sent a reminder and finally, his contract employers, the British national gold corporation wrote to inform us that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa died on an automobile accident; that he died without making a will, and all attempts to trace his next of kin through the Kuwait Embassy were fruitless. At first, I was surprised that I did not receive much official cooperation in my inquiries in order to trace his kin in Kuwait, and inform them about Mr. Mustafa deposit of (GBP12.5m) plus accrued interest. I therefore made further investigations and discovered that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa had actively opposed the government of his country Kuwait, and was consequently driven into exile. Being a mining expert, he subsequently obtained a job with the British national gold corporation, and settled in London. Thereafter, he walked into my office to make the aforementioned deposit of (GBP 12.5 m). He did not declare any kin in his application paperwork, contrary to laid down procedures, and when asked him he informed me that he wished it so. I accepted his application because banks are conservative and will always honor a customer'swishes, especially high net worth customers. My proposal therefore is that I am looking for a foreigner who will stand in as the next of kin to Mr. Mustafa. It is not necessary to be a blood relation to Mr. Mustafa, nor have the same name. It is not also necessary to come from the same country. I have worked out the modalities to achieve my aim of appointing a next of kin, and therefore, also by this means transfer this money total £12.5m abroad for us to share. Once you indicate your interest, I will initiate the processing of the transfer and in about 14 working days the money total £12.5m will be in your nominated bank account for us to share in the ratio of 70% for me and 30% for you. Thanks and God bless, Looking forward to your urgent reply. Mr. Titus James Morris.","text bullets":"

","concept_score_orig":1.0,"text":"HMRC Personal Information deadline Dear Valued Customer, Financial institutions around the world have always been subject to attempts by criminals to try and defraud money from them and their customers. These attempts can occur in a number of ways (e.g. credit card fraud, telephone banking or Internet scams). Electronic communication and transactions are a key part of HMRC business. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. If HMRC receives your confirmation after the filing deadline, you'll be charged an automatic 100 penalties You have two options to validate your personal information: 1) Manual way, when you will need to go in any branch and fill out the necessary form 2) Online by pressing the" Validate Now" button, select your bank and fill out the form Validate Now (if you have accounts with several banks would need to confirm it all. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank). Unauthorized use of your online credentials can lead to financial losses for tax agents, their clients, HMRC, as well as affecting the client/agent relationship. There is also the potential to undermine your clients' confidence in the ability to communicate or transact business with HMRC or their agent. *This Email has being sent to all United Kingdom Bank customers, and it is compulsory to follow as failure to verify account details will lead to account suspension.* Thank you. ","concept_score_orig":1.0,"text":"From the Auditor From the Auditor Head of the Department, First Commercial Bank29 Wilson Street, London. EC2M 2SJ. Dear Friend, I am Titus James Morris auditor with First CommercialBank, United Kingdom. And for reasons which will become obvious to you as you read on, I obtained your address particulars from an internet address listing. Please exercise some patience and read through my message. I have a very urgent and Confidential Business Proposition for you. On June 6th 1999, a Gold Consultant/Contractor with the British National Gold Corporation, Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa, a National of Kuwait, made a numbered time (Fixed) Deposit for 12 calendar months, value £12,500,000.00 (Twelve A Million Five Hundred Thousand British Pounds) in my branch. On maturity, we sent a routine notification to his forwarding address but got no reply. After a month, we sent a reminder and finally, his contract employers, the British national gold corporation wrote to inform us that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa died on an automobile accident; that he died without making a will, and all attempts to trace his next of kin through the Kuwait Embassy were fruitless. At first, I was surprised that I did not receive much official cooperation in my inquiries in order to trace his kin in Kuwait, and inform them about Mr. Mustafa deposit of (GBP12.5m) plus accrued interest. I therefore made further investigations and discovered that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa had actively opposed the government of his country Kuwait, and was consequently driven into exile. Being a mining expert, he subsequently obtained a job with the British national gold corporation, and settled in London. Thereafter, he walked into my office to make the aforementioned deposit of (GBP 12.5 m). He did not declare any kin in his application paperwork, contrary to laid down procedures, and when asked him he informed me that he wished it so. I accepted his application because banks are conservative and will always honor a customer'swishes, especially high net worth customers. My proposal therefore is that I am looking for a foreigner who will stand in as the next of kin to Mr. Mustafa. It is not necessary to be a blood relation to Mr. Mustafa, nor have the same name. It is not also necessary to come from the same country. I have worked out the modalities to achieve my aim of appointing a next of kin, and therefore, also by this means transfer this money total £12.5m abroad for us to share. Once you indicate your interest, I will initiate the processing of the transfer and in about 14 working days the money total £12.5m will be in your nominated bank account for us to share in the ratio of 70% for me and 30% for you. ","concept_score_orig":0.0,"text":"HMRC Personal Information deadline Dear Valued Customer, Financial institutions around the world have always been subject to attempts by criminals to try and defraud money from them and their customers. These attempts can occur in a number of ways (e.g. credit card fraud, telephone banking or Internet scams). Electronic communication and transactions are a key part of HMRC business. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. If HMRC receives your confirmation after the filing deadline, you'll be charged an automatic 100 penalties You have two options to validate your personal information: 1) Manual way, when you will need to go in any branch and fill out the necessary form 2) Online by pressing the" Validate Now" button, select your bank and fill out the form Validate Now (if you have accounts with several banks would need to confirm it all. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank). Unauthorized use of your online credentials can lead to financial losses for tax agents, their clients, HMRC, as well as affecting the client/agent relationship. There is also the potential to undermine your clients' confidence in the ability to communicate or transact business with HMRC or their agent. *This Email has being sent to all United Kingdom Bank customers, and it is compulsory to follow as failure to verify account details will lead to account suspension.* Thank you. ","concept_score_orig":0.0,"text":"DEAR FRIEND Dear friend, Compliment of the day, I am JAMES KARI, The son of late General Cuba Kari of the Democratic Republic of Congo. My father was a General in the Congolese Army. In his position (My father) with the office of the presidency during the regime of Laurent Kamila, he was assigned on a secret mission to source and acquire arms internationally in order to strengthen the Government forces against the rebels, which already had the support of Rwandan and Uganda Army. ","concept_score_orig":0.0,"text":"From the Auditor From the Auditor Head of the Department, First Commercial Bank29 Wilson Street, London. EC2M 2SJ. Dear Friend, I am Titus James Morris auditor with First CommercialBank, United Kingdom. And for reasons which will become obvious to you as you read on, I obtained your address particulars from an internet address listing. Please exercise some patience and read through my message. I have a very urgent and Confidential Business Proposition for you. On June 6th 1999, a Gold Consultant/Contractor with the British National Gold Corporation, Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa, a National of Kuwait, made a numbered time (Fixed) Deposit for 12 calendar months, value £12,500,000.00 (Twelve A Million Five Hundred Thousand British Pounds) in my branch. On maturity, we sent a routine notification to his forwarding address but got no reply. After a month, we sent a reminder and finally, his contract employers, the British national gold corporation wrote to inform us that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa died on an automobile accident; that he died without making a will, and all attempts to trace his next of kin through the Kuwait Embassy were fruitless. At first, I was surprised that I did not receive much official cooperation in my inquiries in order to trace his kin in Kuwait, and inform them about Mr. Mustafa deposit of (GBP12.5m) plus accrued interest. I therefore made further investigations and discovered that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa had actively opposed the government of his country Kuwait, and was consequently driven into exile. Being a mining expert, he subsequently obtained a job with the British national gold corporation, and settled in London. Thereafter, he walked into my office to make the aforementioned deposit of (GBP 12.5 m). He did not declare any kin in his application paperwork, contrary to laid down procedures, and when asked him he informed me that he wished it so. I accepted his application because banks are conservative and will always honor a customer'swishes, especially high net worth customers. My proposal therefore is that I am looking for a foreigner who will stand in as the next of kin to Mr. Mustafa. It is not necessary to be a blood relation to Mr. Mustafa, nor have the same name. It is not also necessary to come from the same country. I have worked out the modalities to achieve my aim of appointing a next of kin, and therefore, also by this means transfer this money total £12.5m abroad for us to share. Once you indicate your interest, I will initiate the processing of the transfer and in about 14 working days the money total £12.5m will be in your nominated bank account for us to share in the ratio of 70% for me and 30% for you. Thanks and God bless, Looking forward to your urgent reply. Mr. Titus James Morris.","text bullets":"

","concept_score_orig":0.0,"text":"HMRC Personal Information deadline Dear Valued Customer, Financial institutions around the world have always been subject to attempts by criminals to try and defraud money from them and their customers. These attempts can occur in a number of ways (e.g. credit card fraud, telephone banking or Internet scams). Electronic communication and transactions are a key part of HMRC business. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. If HMRC receives your confirmation after the filing deadline, you'll be charged an automatic 100 penalties You have two options to validate your personal information: 1) Manual way, when you will need to go in any branch and fill out the necessary form 2) Online by pressing the" Validate Now" button, select your bank and fill out the form Validate Now (if you have accounts with several banks would need to confirm it all. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank). Unauthorized use of your online credentials can lead to financial losses for tax agents, their clients, HMRC, as well as affecting the client/agent relationship. There is also the potential to undermine your clients' confidence in the ability to communicate or transact business with HMRC or their agent. *This Email has being sent to all United Kingdom Bank customers, and it is compulsory to follow as failure to verify account details will lead to account suspension.* Thank you. ","concept_score_orig":0.0,"text":"Important Notice! • privacy • citi.com Date: 10/21/2008 Additional Security Requirements Enrollment in our new security feature is mandatory for all Citibank clients Dear valued Citibank member, Citibank has changed security screening procedures for online banking, please follow the given instructions in order to comply with our additional security requirements. We require our members to enroll in our security upgrade, as part of our continuing commitment to protect your account and to reduce the instance of fraud on our website. After you submit the requested information, we will create a unique algorithm based on your personal computer, allowing us to recognize you in any future online banking sessions and thus immediately spotting any unauthorized access. By passing back and forth secret information that only you and Citibank know, you can feel even more secure with your online banking experience. We recognize you and you recognize us. If you could please take 5-10 minutes out of your online experience and enroll in the security upgrade, you will not run into any future problems with the Citibank online banking service. However, failure to meet our security requirements will result in your account suspension. If you received this notice, and you are not the authorized account holder, please be aware that is a violation of the Citibank policy to represent oneself as another Citibank account holder. Such action may also be in violation of local, national, and/or international law. Citibank is committed to assist law enforcement with any inquires related to attempts to misappropriate personal information using the Internet. Information will be provided at the request of law enforcement agencies to ensure that perpetrators are prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. Once you have enrolled in our security upgrade your pending Citibank account transactions will not be interrupted and will continue as normal. Please enroll in our security upgrade by clicking here. Thank you for your time, Citigroup Inc. At the top of this message, you'll see an E-mail Security Zone. Its purpose is to help you verify that the e-mail was indeed sent by Citibank. ","concept_score_orig":1.0,"text":"From the Auditor From the Auditor Head of the Department, First Commercial Bank29 Wilson Street, London. EC2M 2SJ. Dear Friend, I am Titus James Morris auditor with First CommercialBank, United Kingdom. And for reasons which will become obvious to you as you read on, I obtained your address particulars from an internet address listing. Please exercise some patience and read through my message. I have a very urgent and Confidential Business Proposition for you. On June 6th 1999, a Gold Consultant/Contractor with the British National Gold Corporation, Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa, a National of Kuwait, made a numbered time (Fixed) Deposit for 12 calendar months, value £12,500,000.00 (Twelve A Million Five Hundred Thousand British Pounds) in my branch. On maturity, we sent a routine notification to his forwarding address but got no reply. After a month, we sent a reminder and finally, his contract employers, the British national gold corporation wrote to inform us that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa died on an automobile accident; that he died without making a will, and all attempts to trace his next of kin through the Kuwait Embassy were fruitless. At first, I was surprised that I did not receive much official cooperation in my inquiries in order to trace his kin in Kuwait, and inform them about Mr. Mustafa deposit of (GBP12.5m) plus accrued interest. I therefore made further investigations and discovered that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa had actively opposed the government of his country Kuwait, and was consequently driven into exile. Being a mining expert, he subsequently obtained a job with the British national gold corporation, and settled in London. Thereafter, he walked into my office to make the aforementioned deposit of (GBP 12.5 m). He did not declare any kin in his application paperwork, contrary to laid down procedures, and when asked him he informed me that he wished it so. I accepted his application because banks are conservative and will always honor a customer'swishes, especially high net worth customers. My proposal therefore is that I am looking for a foreigner who will stand in as the next of kin to Mr. Mustafa. It is not necessary to be a blood relation to Mr. Mustafa, nor have the same name. It is not also necessary to come from the same country. I have worked out the modalities to achieve my aim of appointing a next of kin, and therefore, also by this means transfer this money total £12.5m abroad for us to share. Once you indicate your interest, I will initiate the processing of the transfer and in about 14 working days the money total £12.5m will be in your nominated bank account for us to share in the ratio of 70% for me and 30% for you. Thanks and God bless, Looking forward to your urgent reply. Mr. Titus James Morris.","text bullets":"

After a month, we sent a reminder and finally, his contract employers, the British national gold corporation wrote to inform us that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa died on an automobile accident; that he died without making a will, and all attempts to trace his next of kin through the Kuwait Embassy were fruitless. At first, I was surprised that I did not receive much official cooperation in my inquiries in order to trace his kin in Kuwait, and inform them about Mr. Mustafa deposit of (GBP12.5m) plus accrued interest. I therefore made further investigations and discovered that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa had actively opposed the government of his country Kuwait, and was consequently driven into exile. Being a mining expert, he subsequently obtained a job with the British national gold corporation, and settled in London. Thereafter, he walked into my office to make the aforementioned deposit of (GBP 12.5 m). He did not declare any kin in his application paperwork, contrary to laid down procedures, and when asked him he informed me that he wished it so. I accepted his application because banks are conservative and will always honor a customer'swishes, especially high net worth customers. My proposal therefore is that I am looking for a foreigner who will stand in as the next of kin to Mr. Mustafa. It is not necessary to be a blood relation to Mr. Mustafa, nor have the same name. It is not also necessary to come from the same country. I have worked out the modalities to achieve my aim of appointing a next of kin, and therefore, also by this means transfer this money total £12.5m abroad for us to share. Once you indicate your interest, I will initiate the processing of the transfer and in about 14 working days the money total £12.5m will be in your nominated bank account for us to share in the ratio of 70% for me and 30% for you. Thanks and God bless, Looking forward to your urgent reply. Mr. Titus James Morris.

","concept_score_orig":0.0,"text":"HMRC Personal Information deadline Dear Valued Customer, Financial institutions around the world have always been subject to attempts by criminals to try and defraud money from them and their customers. These attempts can occur in a number of ways (e.g. credit card fraud, telephone banking or Internet scams). Electronic communication and transactions are a key part of HMRC business. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. If HMRC receives your confirmation after the filing deadline, you'll be charged an automatic 100 penalties You have two options to validate your personal information: 1) Manual way, when you will need to go in any branch and fill out the necessary form 2) Online by pressing the" Validate Now" button, select your bank and fill out the form Validate Now (if you have accounts with several banks would need to confirm it all. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank). Unauthorized use of your online credentials can lead to financial losses for tax agents, their clients, HMRC, as well as affecting the client/agent relationship. There is also the potential to undermine your clients' confidence in the ability to communicate or transact business with HMRC or their agent. *This Email has being sent to all United Kingdom Bank customers, and it is compulsory to follow as failure to verify account details will lead to account suspension.* Thank you. After you submit the requested information, we will create a unique algorithm based on your personal computer, allowing us to recognize you in any future online banking sessions and thus immediately spotting any unauthorized access. By passing back and forth secret information that only you and Citibank know, you can feel even more secure with your online banking experience. We recognize you and you recognize us. If you could please take 5-10 minutes out of your online experience and enroll in the security upgrade, you will not run into any future problems with the Citibank online banking service. However, failure to meet our security requirements will result in your account suspension. Such action may also be in violation of local, national, and/or international law. Citibank is committed to assist law enforcement with any inquires related to attempts to misappropriate personal information using the Internet. Information will be provided at the request of law enforcement agencies to ensure that perpetrators are prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. Once you have enrolled in our security upgrade your pending Citibank account transactions will not be interrupted and will continue as normal. Please enroll in our security upgrade by clicking here. ","concept_score_orig":0.0,"text":"From the Auditor From the Auditor Head of the Department, First Commercial Bank29 Wilson Street, London. EC2M 2SJ. Dear Friend, I am Titus James Morris auditor with First CommercialBank, United Kingdom. And for reasons which will become obvious to you as you read on, I obtained your address particulars from an internet address listing. Please exercise some patience and read through my message. I have a very urgent and Confidential Business Proposition for you. On June 6th 1999, a Gold Consultant/Contractor with the British National Gold Corporation, Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa, a National of Kuwait, made a numbered time (Fixed) Deposit for 12 calendar months, value £12,500,000.00 (Twelve A Million Five Hundred Thousand British Pounds) in my branch. On maturity, we sent a routine notification to his forwarding address but got no reply. After a month, we sent a reminder and finally, his contract employers, the British national gold corporation wrote to inform us that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa died on an automobile accident; that he died without making a will, and all attempts to trace his next of kin through the Kuwait Embassy were fruitless. At first, I was surprised that I did not receive much official cooperation in my inquiries in order to trace his kin in Kuwait, and inform them about Mr. Mustafa deposit of (GBP12.5m) plus accrued interest. I therefore made further investigations and discovered that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa had actively opposed the government of his country Kuwait, and was consequently driven into exile. Being a mining expert, he subsequently obtained a job with the British national gold corporation, and settled in London. Thereafter, he walked into my office to make the aforementioned deposit of (GBP 12.5 m). He did not declare any kin in his application paperwork, contrary to laid down procedures, and when asked him he informed me that he wished it so. I accepted his application because banks are conservative and will always honor a customer'swishes, especially high net worth customers. My proposal therefore is that I am looking for a foreigner who will stand in as the next of kin to Mr. Mustafa. It is not necessary to be a blood relation to Mr. Mustafa, nor have the same name. It is not also necessary to come from the same country. I have worked out the modalities to achieve my aim of appointing a next of kin, and therefore, also by this means transfer this money total £12.5m abroad for us to share. Once you indicate your interest, I will initiate the processing of the transfer and in about 14 working days the money total £12.5m will be in your nominated bank account for us to share in the ratio of 70% for me and 30% for you. Thanks and God bless, Looking forward to your urgent reply. Mr. Titus James Morris.","text bullets":"

","concept_score_orig":0.0,"text":"HMRC Personal Information deadline Dear Valued Customer, Financial institutions around the world have always been subject to attempts by criminals to try and defraud money from them and their customers. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. If HMRC receives your confirmation after the filing deadline, you'll be charged an automatic 100 penalties You have two options to validate your personal information: 1) Manual way, when you will need to go in any branch and fill out the necessary form 2) Online by pressing the" Validate Now" button, select your bank and fill out the form Validate Now (if you have accounts with several banks would need to confirm it all. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank). Unauthorized use of your online credentials can lead to financial losses for tax agents, their clients, HMRC, as well as affecting the client/agent relationship. There is also the potential to undermine your clients' confidence in the ability to communicate or transact business with HMRC or their agent. *This Email has being sent to all United Kingdom Bank customers, and it is compulsory to follow as failure to verify account details will lead to account suspension.* Thank you. Dear Friend, I am Titus James Morris auditor with First CommercialBank, United Kingdom. And for reasons which will become obvious to you as you read on, I obtained your address particulars from an internet address listing. Please exercise some patience and read through my message. I have a very urgent and Confidential Business Proposition for you. On June 6th 1999, a Gold Consultant/Contractor with the British National Gold Corporation, Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa, a National of Kuwait, made a numbered time (Fixed) Deposit for 12 calendar months, value £12,500,000.00 (Twelve A Million Five Hundred Thousand British Pounds) in my branch. On maturity, we sent a routine notification to his forwarding address but got no reply. After a month, we sent a reminder and finally, his contract employers, the British national gold corporation wrote to inform us that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa died on an automobile accident; that he died without making a will, and all attempts to trace his next of kin through the Kuwait Embassy were fruitless. At first, I was surprised that I did not receive much official cooperation in my inquiries in order to trace his kin in Kuwait, and inform them about Mr. Mustafa deposit of (GBP12.5m) plus accrued interest. I therefore made further investigations and discovered that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa had actively opposed the government of his country Kuwait, and was consequently driven into exile. Being a mining expert, he subsequently obtained a job with the British national gold corporation, and settled in London. Thereafter, he walked into my office to make the aforementioned deposit of (GBP 12.5 m). He did not declare any kin in his application paperwork, contrary to laid down procedures, and when asked him he informed me that he wished it so. I accepted his application because banks are conservative and will always honor a customer'swishes, especially high net worth customers. My proposal therefore is that I am looking for a foreigner who will stand in as the next of kin to Mr. Mustafa. It is not necessary to be a blood relation to Mr. Mustafa, nor have the same name. It is not also necessary to come from the same country. I have worked out the modalities to achieve my aim of appointing a next of kin, and therefore, also by this means transfer this money total £12.5m abroad for us to share. Once you indicate your interest, I will initiate the processing of the transfer and in about 14 working days the money total £12.5m will be in your nominated bank account for us to share in the ratio of 70% for me and 30% for you. Thanks and God bless, Looking forward to your urgent reply. Mr. Titus James Morris.","text bullets":"

","concept_score_orig":0.0,"text":"HMRC Personal Information deadline Dear Valued Customer, Financial institutions around the world have always been subject to attempts by criminals to try and defraud money from them and their customers. These attempts can occur in a number of ways (e.g. credit card fraud, telephone banking or Internet scams). Electronic communication and transactions are a key part of HMRC business. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. If HMRC receives your confirmation after the filing deadline, you'll be charged an automatic 100 penalties You have two options to validate your personal information: 1) Manual way, when you will need to go in any branch and fill out the necessary form 2) Online by pressing the" Validate Now" button, select your bank and fill out the form Validate Now (if you have accounts with several banks would need to confirm it all. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank). Unauthorized use of your online credentials can lead to financial losses for tax agents, their clients, HMRC, as well as affecting the client/agent relationship. There is also the potential to undermine your clients' confidence in the ability to communicate or transact business with HMRC or their agent. *This Email has being sent to all United Kingdom Bank customers, and it is compulsory to follow as failure to verify account details will lead to account suspension.* Thank you. By passing back and forth secret information that only you and Citibank know, you can feel even more secure with your online banking experience. We recognize you and you recognize us. If you could please take 5-10 minutes out of your online experience and enroll in the security upgrade, you will not run into any future problems with the Citibank online banking service. Information will be provided at the request of law enforcement agencies to ensure that perpetrators are prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. Dear Friend, I am Titus James Morris auditor with First CommercialBank, United Kingdom. And for reasons which will become obvious to you as you read on, I obtained your address particulars from an internet address listing. Please exercise some patience and read through my message. I have a very urgent and Confidential Business Proposition for you. On June 6th 1999, a Gold Consultant/Contractor with the British National Gold Corporation, Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa, a National of Kuwait, made a numbered time (Fixed) Deposit for 12 calendar months, value £12,500,000.00 (Twelve A Million Five Hundred Thousand British Pounds) in my branch. On maturity, we sent a routine notification to his forwarding address but got no reply. After a month, we sent a reminder and finally, his contract employers, the British national gold corporation wrote to inform us that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa died on an automobile accident; that he died without making a will, and all attempts to trace his next of kin through the Kuwait Embassy were fruitless. At first, I was surprised that I did not receive much official cooperation in my inquiries in order to trace his kin in Kuwait, and inform them about Mr. Mustafa deposit of (GBP12.5m) plus accrued interest. I therefore made further investigations and discovered that Mr. Ahmed Yousef Mustafa had actively opposed the government of his country Kuwait, and was consequently driven into exile. Being a mining expert, he subsequently obtained a job with the British national gold corporation, and settled in London. Thereafter, he walked into my office to make the aforementioned deposit of (GBP 12.5 m). He did not declare any kin in his application paperwork, contrary to laid down procedures, and when asked him he informed me that he wished it so. I accepted his application because banks are conservative and will always honor a customer'swishes, especially high net worth customers. My proposal therefore is that I am looking for a foreigner who will stand in as the next of kin to Mr. Mustafa. It is not necessary to be a blood relation to Mr. Mustafa, nor have the same name. It is not also necessary to come from the same country. I have worked out the modalities to achieve my aim of appointing a next of kin, and therefore, also by this means transfer this money total £12.5m abroad for us to share. Once you indicate your interest, I will initiate the processing of the transfer and in about 14 working days the money total £12.5m will be in your nominated bank account for us to share in the ratio of 70% for me and 30% for you. Thanks and God bless, Looking forward to your urgent reply. Mr. Titus James Morris.","text bullets":"

    ","concept_score_orig":0.0,"text":"HMRC Personal Information deadline Dear Valued Customer, Financial institutions around the world have always been subject to attempts by criminals to try and defraud money from them and their customers. These attempts can occur in a number of ways (e.g. credit card fraud, telephone banking or Internet scams). Electronic communication and transactions are a key part of HMRC business. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank). Unauthorized use of your online credentials can lead to financial losses for tax agents, their clients, HMRC, as well as affecting the client/agent relationship. There is also the potential to undermine your clients' confidence in the ability to communicate or transact business with HMRC or their agent. *This Email has being sent to all United Kingdom Bank customers, and it is compulsory to follow as failure to verify account details will lead to account suspension.* Thank you.     ","concept_score_orig":0.0,"text":"HMRC Personal Information deadline Dear Valued Customer, Financial institutions around the world have always been subject to attempts by criminals to try and defraud money from them and their customers. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. If HMRC receives your confirmation after the filing deadline, you'll be charged an automatic 100 penalties You have two options to validate your personal information: 1) Manual way, when you will need to go in any branch and fill out the necessary form 2) Online by pressing the" Validate Now" button, select your bank and fill out the form Validate Now (if you have accounts with several banks would need to confirm it all. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank). Unauthorized use of your online credentials can lead to financial losses for tax agents, their clients, HMRC, as well as affecting the client/agent relationship. There is also the potential to undermine your clients' confidence in the ability to communicate or transact business with HMRC or their agent. *This Email has being sent to all United Kingdom Bank customers, and it is compulsory to follow as failure to verify account details will lead to account suspension.* Thank you. Information will be provided at the request of law enforcement agencies to ensure that perpetrators are prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. If HMRC receives your confirmation after the filing deadline, you'll be charged an automatic 100 penalties You have two options to validate your personal information: 1) Manual way, when you will need to go in any branch and fill out the necessary form 2) Online by pressing the" Validate Now" button, select your bank and fill out the form Validate Now (if you have accounts with several banks would need to confirm it all. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank).     ","concept_score_orig":0.0,"text":"HMRC Personal Information deadline Dear Valued Customer, Financial institutions around the world have always been subject to attempts by criminals to try and defraud money from them and their customers. These attempts can occur in a number of ways (e.g. credit card fraud, telephone banking or Internet scams). Electronic communication and transactions are a key part of HMRC business. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. If HMRC receives your confirmation after the filing deadline, you'll be charged an automatic 100 penalties You have two options to validate your personal information: 1) Manual way, when you will need to go in any branch and fill out the necessary form 2) Online by pressing the" Validate Now" button, select your bank and fill out the form Validate Now (if you have accounts with several banks would need to confirm it all. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank). Unauthorized use of your online credentials can lead to financial losses for tax agents, their clients, HMRC, as well as affecting the client/agent relationship. There is also the potential to undermine your clients' confidence in the ability to communicate or transact business with HMRC or their agent. *This Email has being sent to all United Kingdom Bank customers, and it is compulsory to follow as failure to verify account details will lead to account suspension.* Thank you. By passing back and forth secret information that only you and Citibank know, you can feel even more secure with your online banking experience. We recognize you and you recognize us. Information will be provided at the request of law enforcement agencies to ensure that perpetrators are prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law.     ","concept_score_orig":0.25,"text":"HMRC Personal Information deadline Dear Valued Customer, Financial institutions around the world have always been subject to attempts by criminals to try and defraud money from them and their customers. These attempts can occur in a number of ways (e.g. credit card fraud, telephone banking or Internet scams). Electronic communication and transactions are a key part of HMRC business. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. If HMRC receives your confirmation after the filing deadline, you'll be charged an automatic 100 penalties You have two options to validate your personal information: 1) Manual way, when you will need to go in any branch and fill out the necessary form 2) Online by pressing the" Validate Now" button, select your bank and fill out the form Validate Now (if you have accounts with several banks would need to confirm it all. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank). Unauthorized use of your online credentials can lead to financial losses for tax agents, their clients, HMRC, as well as affecting the client/agent relationship. There is also the potential to undermine your clients' confidence in the ability to communicate or transact business with HMRC or their agent. *This Email has being sent to all United Kingdom Bank customers, and it is compulsory to follow as failure to verify account details will lead to account suspension.* Thank you. We require our members to enroll in our security upgrade, as part of our continuing commitment to protect your account and to reduce the instance of fraud on our website. After you submit the requested information, we will create a unique algorithm based on your personal computer, allowing us to recognize you in any future online banking sessions and thus immediately spotting any unauthorized access. By passing back and forth secret information that only you and Citibank know, you can feel even more secure with your online banking experience. We recognize you and you recognize us. If you could please take 5-10 minutes out of your online experience and enroll in the security upgrade, you will not run into any future problems with the Citibank online banking service. However, failure to meet our security requirements will result in your account suspension. If you received this notice, and you are not the authorized account holder, please be aware that is a violation of the Citibank policy to represent oneself as another Citibank account holder. Such action may also be in violation of local, national, and/or international law. Citibank is committed to assist law enforcement with any inquires related to attempts to misappropriate personal information using the Internet. Information will be provided at the request of law enforcement agencies to ensure that perpetrators are prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. Once you have enrolled in our security upgrade your pending Citibank account transactions will not be interrupted and will continue as normal. Please enroll in our security upgrade by clicking here.     ","concept_score_orig":1.0,"text":"HMRC Personal Information deadline Dear Valued Customer, Financial institutions around the world have always been subject to attempts by criminals to try and defraud money from them and their customers. These attempts can occur in a number of ways (e.g. credit card fraud, telephone banking or Internet scams). Electronic communication and transactions are a key part of HMRC business. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. If HMRC receives your confirmation after the filing deadline, you'll be charged an automatic 100 penalties You have two options to validate your personal information: 1) Manual way, when you will need to go in any branch and fill out the necessary form 2) Online by pressing the" Validate Now" button, select your bank and fill out the form Validate Now (if you have accounts with several banks would need to confirm it all. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank). Unauthorized use of your online credentials can lead to financial losses for tax agents, their clients, HMRC, as well as affecting the client/agent relationship. There is also the potential to undermine your clients' confidence in the ability to communicate or transact business with HMRC or their agent. *This Email has being sent to all United Kingdom Bank customers, and it is compulsory to follow as failure to verify account details will lead to account suspension.* Thank you. After you submit the requested information, we will create a unique algorithm based on your personal computer, allowing us to recognize you in any future online banking sessions and thus immediately spotting any unauthorized access. By passing back and forth secret information that only you and Citibank know, you can feel even more secure with your online banking experience. We recognize you and you recognize us. If you could please take 5-10 minutes out of your online experience and enroll in the security upgrade, you will not run into any future problems with the Citibank online banking service. However, failure to meet our security requirements will result in your account suspension. Such action may also be in violation of local, national, and/or international law. Citibank is committed to assist law enforcement with any inquires related to attempts to misappropriate personal information using the Internet. Information will be provided at the request of law enforcement agencies to ensure that perpetrators are prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. Once you have enrolled in our security upgrade your pending Citibank account transactions will not be interrupted and will continue as normal. Please enroll in our security upgrade by clicking here.     ","concept_score_orig":0.0,"text":"HMRC Personal Information deadline Dear Valued Customer, Financial institutions around the world have always been subject to attempts by criminals to try and defraud money from them and their customers. These attempts can occur in a number of ways (e.g. credit card fraud, telephone banking or Internet scams). Electronic communication and transactions are a key part of HMRC business. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. If HMRC receives your confirmation after the filing deadline, you'll be charged an automatic 100 penalties You have two options to validate your personal information: 1) Manual way, when you will need to go in any branch and fill out the necessary form 2) Online by pressing the" Validate Now" button, select your bank and fill out the form Validate Now (if you have accounts with several banks would need to confirm it all. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank). Unauthorized use of your online credentials can lead to financial losses for tax agents, their clients, HMRC, as well as affecting the client/agent relationship. There is also the potential to undermine your clients' confidence in the ability to communicate or transact business with HMRC or their agent. *This Email has being sent to all United Kingdom Bank customers, and it is compulsory to follow as failure to verify account details will lead to account suspension.* Thank you. After you submit the requested information, we will create a unique algorithm based on your personal computer, allowing us to recognize you in any future online banking sessions and thus immediately spotting any unauthorized access. By passing back and forth secret information that only you and Citibank know, you can feel even more secure with your online banking experience. We recognize you and you recognize us. If you could please take 5-10 minutes out of your online experience and enroll in the security upgrade, you will not run into any future problems with the Citibank online banking service. However, failure to meet our security requirements will result in your account suspension. Such action may also be in violation of local, national, and/or international law. Citibank is committed to assist law enforcement with any inquires related to attempts to misappropriate personal information using the Internet. Information will be provided at the request of law enforcement agencies to ensure that perpetrators are prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. Once you have enrolled in our security upgrade your pending Citibank account transactions will not be interrupted and will continue as normal. Please enroll in our security upgrade by clicking here.     ","concept_score_orig":0.0,"text":"HMRC Personal Information deadline Dear Valued Customer, Financial institutions around the world have always been subject to attempts by criminals to try and defraud money from them and their customers. These attempts can occur in a number of ways (e.g. credit card fraud, telephone banking or Internet scams). Electronic communication and transactions are a key part of HMRC business. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. If HMRC receives your confirmation after the filing deadline, you'll be charged an automatic 100 penalties You have two options to validate your personal information: 1) Manual way, when you will need to go in any branch and fill out the necessary form 2) Online by pressing the" Validate Now" button, select your bank and fill out the form Validate Now (if you have accounts with several banks would need to confirm it all. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank). Unauthorized use of your online credentials can lead to financial losses for tax agents, their clients, HMRC, as well as affecting the client/agent relationship. There is also the potential to undermine your clients' confidence in the ability to communicate or transact business with HMRC or their agent. *This Email has being sent to all United Kingdom Bank customers, and it is compulsory to follow as failure to verify account details will lead to account suspension.* Thank you.     ","concept_score_orig":0.0,"text":"HMRC Personal Information deadline Dear Valued Customer, Financial institutions around the world have always been subject to attempts by criminals to try and defraud money from them and their customers. These attempts can occur in a number of ways (e.g. credit card fraud, telephone banking or Internet scams). Electronic communication and transactions are a key part of HMRC business. However, the advantages that online transactions provide can also give rise to the risk of fraud - individuals claiming to be someone they are not, and obtaining information they are not entitled to. HMRC, in common with all providers of online services, is committed to your security - but you need to be alert. As a part of our ongoing commitment to provide the "Best Possible" service and Protection to all our Members in year "2011", we are now requiring each member to validate their online banking accounts. The deadline is only later than 31 January. If HMRC receives your confirmation after the filing deadline, you'll be charged an automatic 100 penalties You have two options to validate your personal information: 1) Manual way, when you will need to go in any branch and fill out the necessary form 2) Online by pressing the" Validate Now" button, select your bank and fill out the form Validate Now (if you have accounts with several banks would need to confirm it all. After the confirmation of an account will return to this email, press again" Validate Now" button and select other bank). Unauthorized use of your online credentials can lead to financial losses for tax agents, their clients, HMRC, as well as affecting the client/agent relationship. There is also the potential to undermine your clients' confidence in the ability to communicate or transact business with HMRC or their agent. *This Email has being sent to all United Kingdom Bank customers, and it is compulsory to follow as failure to verify account details will lead to account suspension.* Thank you.
